messages:
maria_support: Customer acct_444 is seeing intermittent 429s + high tail latency on /v1/generate-chat since ~12:10 PT. They say it happens when hitting model `gpt-open-8k` in bursts from a batch job. Can we triage?

opsbot: :warning: Alert fired: quota-exhaustion-high for tenant acct_444 — 429 rate > 0.8% over 2m (rule: tenant.429_rate > 0.5% && window=2m). link: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/alert-8842

maria_support: Pasting a stripped sample log from their request: 
```
request_id=01G6X1JZ4Y sample_ts=2026-03-15T19:12:07Z tenant=acct_444 route=/v1/generate-chat model=gpt-open-8k status=429 latency_ms=1324 tokens_in=12 tokens_out=48
```
They also provided a curl repro snippet: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate-chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"short prompt"}],"max_tokens":64}'
```

maria_support: Customer claims they were running 120rps for ~90s, then drop to 250rps for a minute, spike again. They think our burst window didn't cover it.

dylan_sre: Thanks — first steps: 1) check per-tenant 429-by-route and 429-by-model panel for acct_444, 2) correlate with token_rate and committed_capacity metrics, 3) pull traces for a few request_ids.

dylan_sre: Kibana quick query I used: `index: requests-* tenant_id:acct_444 AND status:429 AND @timestamp:[now-15m TO now]` — will show burst timestamps. Also check `token_bucket_fill{tenant="acct_444"}` in Prometheus.

ken_prod: I pulled the grafana view: https://console.redwood.ai/grafana/d/tenant-quota/acct_444 — seeing a sharp token_rate spike at 19:11:40Z that exceeds the committed_burst_rate. The token bucket goes to 0 for ~22s, matching 429s. Model-level breakdown shows most requests hitting `gpt-open-8k` with small prompt size, so tokens/request low but qps high.

maria_support: Customer says their job intentionally spikes for short windows. Is that considered quota exhaustion (expected) or a bug in our burst math?

evan_infra: Likely quota exhaustion — our burst policy allows short bursts but only up to configured `burst_capacity` and refill rate. If their peak >> burst_capacity, token bucket will deplete and cause 429. Check `quota_config` for acct_444: `commit_qps: 50, burst_capacity: 200`. If they hit 120rps sustained for >1m, they will exhaust.

dylan_sre: Attribution checklist I ran: 
- Confirmed 429s map to token_bucket==0 (Prometheus sample)
- Verified route `/v1/generate-chat` is charged correctly (per-token billing)
- Checked for model fallback logs (none)
- Correlated consumer request IDs -> stack traces (no infra errors)
So this is tenant quota exhaustion, not a runtime bug.

maria_support: Good. Customer asked what immediate mitigations we can offer.

dylan_sre: Options: 
1) Short term: bump their `burst_capacity` or `commit_qps` (requires billing/plan change), or enable permissive burst for N mins (manual override).
2) Medium term: advise they batch requests or throttle to keep sustained qps <= commit_qps.
3) Auto-suggest fallback model: route heavy bursts to a cheaper `gpt-compact-8k` variant to reduce token burn.

ken_prod: I created a ticket to the billing team to propose a temporary burst uplift while they adjust their job. Ticket: BILL-4512.

maria_support: Can we also improve observability so customers can self-diagnose? They asked for a tenant-facing breakdown doc.

evan_infra: Notes to add to docs/console: 
- A tenant dashboard with panels: 429 rate (by route/model), token_bucket_fill, commit_qps vs observed_qps, per-request token histogram.
- Alert recommendation: 429_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m OR token_bucket_fill == 0 for >30s.
- Deep-link example: Console -> Tenant -> Metrics -> Filter `tenant=acct_444` shows the same.

dylan_sre: I'll add a short runbook snippet for support: 
```
1) Ask for request_ids and sample timestamps
2) Run Kibana query for status:429 and tenant_id
3) Check Prometheus: token_bucket_fill{tenant="X"}, committed_qps{tenant="X"}
4) If token_bucket==0 -> quota exhaustion; propose burst bump or throttling
5) If token_bucket>0 -> dig into runtime errors/traces
```

maria_support: Perfect. I'll reply to the customer with the diagnosis (quota exhaustion) + repro steps and the temporary uplift option. I'll reference the grafana link and the ticket BILL-4512. :white_check_mark:

dylan_sre: Leave a note here when the customer confirms either they throttle or accept uplift. We should also follow up to add tenant-level self-serve quota visibility.

maria_support: Will do. Closing the thread for now — will update with customer decision. :wave:
